name: Point-and-figure triple top with vertical count target
note: A high/low point-and-figure grid with box b = box_atr * ATR(pf_atr_n), pinned for a block of box_sessions sessions (the daily rule is 'first trading day of the month'; a session block is the honest intraday equivalent) and a rev_boxes reversal. Entry is the classic triple top: the live X column posts a box strictly above the tops of the tops-1 preceding X columns, which needs several completed columns of structure rather than a single new high. The exit is what makes this family its own thing: a VERTICAL COUNT price objective. At the breakout, count the boxes N in the breakout column measured from that column's own bottom and set the target at bottom + N * b * vc_mult, so the profit objective is a function of the congestion height that was just cleared rather than of ATR, an R multiple or an indicator flip. The other exit leg is structural: a double-bottom breakdown (an O column printing one box below the preceding O column's low) kills a long, a double top covers a short. No ATR stop and no ATR target are set, because the 3-box reversal already embeds a rev_boxes * box_atr * ATR filter and the count is the whole point. Sibling of b001-point-and-figure-triple-top, which trades the same entry with a purely structural exit; the vertical count and the session-pinned box are the difference, and the pair is the controlled test of whether the count adds anything.
source: Thomas Dorsey, 'Point and Figure Charting' (Wiley) for the triple-top/bottom signals and the vertical count; Jeremy du Plessis, 'The Definitive Guide to Point and Figure' (Harriman House) for the high/low construction method and count mechanics. On formalising chart patterns into testable algorithms: Lo, Mamaysky & Wang, 'Foundations of Technical Analysis', NBER WP 7613 (2000), DOI 10.3386/w7613.

import datetime as _dt


def _sessions(bars):
    """A New York session index for every bar, so the box size can be pinned
    for a block of sessions rather than for a block of bars. Splitting on the
    UTC date would cut a session at 20:00 ET, in the middle of the after-hours
    tape."""
    out = []
    last = None
    s = -1
    for b in bars:
        ts = str(b["t"])
        y = int(ts[0:4]); mo = int(ts[5:7]); d = int(ts[8:10])
        hh = int(ts[11:13]); mi = int(ts[14:16])
        if mo < 3 or mo > 11:
            dst = False
        elif 3 < mo < 11:
            dst = True
        elif mo == 3:
            w = _dt.date(y, 3, 1).weekday()
            fs = 1 + ((6 - w) % 7)
            dst = d >= fs + 7
        else:
            w = _dt.date(y, 11, 1).weekday()
            fs = 1 + ((6 - w) % 7)
            dst = d < fs
        t = _dt.datetime(y, mo, d, hh, mi) - _dt.timedelta(minutes=240 if dst else 300)
        key = (t.year, t.month, t.day)
        if key != last:
            last = key
            s += 1
        out.append(s)
    return out


def _atr(hi, lo, cl, per):
    """Wilder ATR, computed here rather than through ctx.indicator: the chart
    has to be walked start to finish inside family_init, and a Series refuses
    forward reads while ctx is still sitting on bar 0."""
    n = len(hi)
    out = [None] * n
    acc = 0.0
    run = None
    for i in range(n):
        if i == 0:
            tr = hi[0] - lo[0]
        else:
            tr = max(hi[i] - lo[i], abs(hi[i] - cl[i - 1]), abs(lo[i] - cl[i - 1]))
        if i < per:
            acc += tr
            if i == per - 1:
                run = acc / per
                out[i] = run
        else:
            run = (run * (per - 1) + tr) / per
            out[i] = run
    return out


def family_init(ctx):
    """A point-and-figure grid, and the two things this family trades on it.

    ENTRY is du Plessis / Dorsey's triple top: the live X column posts a box
    strictly above the tops of the `tops`-1 preceding X columns. Because the
    chart only advances when price moves a whole box, that needs three
    completed columns of structure, not one new high.

    EXIT is the distinctive part -- the VERTICAL COUNT. At the breakout, count
    the boxes N in the breakout column measured from that column's own bottom;
    the target is bottom + N * b * vc_mult, i.e. a price objective derived from
    the height of the congestion that was just cleared, not from an ATR
    multiple or an R multiple. The structural stop is a double-bottom
    breakdown: an O column printing one box below the previous O column's low.

    Box size b = box_atr * ATR(pf_atr_n), pinned for a block of box_sessions
    sessions (the daily rule is 'first trading day of the month'; on intraday
    bars a session block is the honest equivalent) so the grid does not
    re-scale under the pattern it is measuring.
    """
    bars = ctx.bars
    n = len(bars)
    hi = [float(b["h"]) for b in bars]
    lo = [float(b["l"]) for b in bars]
    cl = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]
    sess = _sessions(bars)

    per = max(2, int(ctx.p.pf_atr_n))
    atr = _atr(hi, lo, cl, per)

    hl = bool(int(ctx.p.method))          # 1 = high/low construction, 0 = close
    up_src = hi if hl else cl
    dn_src = lo if hl else cl

    rev = max(1, int(ctx.p.rev_boxes))
    need = max(1, int(ctx.p.tops) - 1)
    blk = max(1, int(ctx.p.box_sessions))
    k = float(ctx.p.box_atr)
    vm = float(ctx.p.vc_mult)

    long_e = [0] * n
    short_e = [0] * n
    tgt_l = [0.0] * n
    tgt_s = [0.0] * n
    stop_l = [0] * n
    stop_s = [0] * n

    col = 0          # +1 inside an X column, -1 inside an O column
    T = 0.0          # top of the live X column
    D = 0.0          # bottom of the live O column
    base = 0.0       # bottom box of the live X column / top box of the live O
    B = None
    xtops = []
    obots = []
    fx = fo = False
    dtb = dbb = False
    blk_at = -10 ** 9

    for i in range(n):
        a = atr[i]
        if a is None or a <= 0:
            continue
        if B is None or (sess[i] - blk_at) >= blk:
            B = round(k * a, 2)
            if B < 0.01:
                B = 0.01
            blk_at = sess[i]
        if col == 0:
            col = 1
            T = up_src[i]
            base = T
            fx = dtb = False
            continue

        adv_x = adv_o = False
        if col > 0:
            if up_src[i] >= T + B:                     # extension beats reversal
                T = T + int((up_src[i] - T) / B) * B
                adv_x = True
            elif dn_src[i] <= T - rev * B:
                xtops.append(T)
                D = T - int((T - dn_src[i]) / B) * B
                base = T - B                           # top box of the new O col
                col = -1
                fo = dbb = False
                adv_o = True
        else:
            if dn_src[i] <= D - B:
                D = D - int((D - dn_src[i]) / B) * B
                adv_o = True
            elif up_src[i] >= D + rev * B:
                obots.append(D)
                T = D + int((up_src[i] - D) / B) * B
                base = D + B                           # bottom box of the new X
                col = 1
                fx = dtb = False
                adv_x = True

        if adv_x:
            if xtops and not dtb and T > xtops[-1]:
                stop_s[i] = 1                          # double top: covers a short
                dtb = True
            if not fx and len(xtops) >= need and T > max(xtops[-need:]):
                long_e[i] = 1
                boxes = int(round((T - base) / B)) + 1
                tgt_l[i] = base + boxes * B * vm
                fx = True
        if adv_o:
            if obots and not dbb and D < obots[-1]:
                stop_l[i] = 1                          # double bottom: kills a long
                dbb = True
            if not fo and len(obots) >= need and D < min(obots[-need:]):
                short_e[i] = 1
                boxes = int(round((base - D) / B)) + 1
                tgt_s[i] = D - boxes * B * vm
                fo = True

    ctx.pf_l = ctx.series(long_e, "pf_long")
    ctx.pf_s = ctx.series(short_e, "pf_short")
    ctx.pf_tl = ctx.series(tgt_l, "pf_target_long")
    ctx.pf_ts = ctx.series(tgt_s, "pf_target_short")
    ctx.pf_xl = ctx.series(stop_l, "pf_stop_long")
    ctx.pf_xs = ctx.series(stop_s, "pf_stop_short")


def signal(ctx, i):
    if ctx.pf_l[i]:
        return 1
    if ctx.pf_s[i]:
        return -1
    return 0


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    """Whichever fires first: the vertical count target is touched, or the
    structural stop prints. The target belongs to the breakout column, which is
    bar entry_i - 1 -- a decision on bar t fills at t+1's open."""
    if not ctx.positions:
        return False
    p = ctx.positions[0]
    j = p["entry_i"] - 1
    if p["side"] == "long":
        if ctx.pf_xl[i]:
            return True
        t = ctx.pf_tl[j] if j >= 0 else 0.0
        return bool(t) and ctx.h[i] >= t
    if ctx.pf_xs[i]:
        return True
    t = ctx.pf_ts[j] if j >= 0 else 0.0
    return bool(t) and ctx.l[i] <= t
